newsitem.title: FRANCE: James Baker ends visit to Polisario in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: James Baker ends visit to Polisario in Algeria.

text.p: The Polisario Front freed 85 Moroccan war prisoners on Sunday as U.N. envoy James Baker arrived at its base in Algeria to discuss the future of the disputed Western Sahara, Algerian state radio reported.

The radio said Polisario leader Mohamed Abdelaziz decided to free the prisoners as a goodwill gesture to help Baker to break an impasse over a U.N. peace plan for the territory largely controlled by Morocco.

Baker, a former U.S. secretary of state, held two meetings with Abdelaziz at the Polisario's main base in the southwestern town of Tindouf before leaving at 5.30. p.m (1630 GMT), the official Algerian news agency APS reported from Tindouf.
It was the last leg of Baker's tour of the North African region to tackle the dispute over control of Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony, which has gone on for more than 20 years.
Baker, who arrived from Mauritania, is on his first visit to the region since U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan appointed him as his personal envoy for Western Sahara last month.
He also visited Morocco and held talks with Algerian leaders in Algiers on what he terms a "fact-finding" mission.
Moroccan troops and Polisario Front guerrillas battled each other in Western Sahara for nearly 16 years before a U.N. ceasefire in September 1991 ended the fighting.

But the second part of a U.N. peace plan, a referendum to enable Saharans to decide whether the territory should be independent or integrate with Morocco, has been held up by arguments over who should be allowed to vote.
APS earlier quoted Polisario foreign minister Bachir Mustapha Sayed as telling reporters in Tindouf that Baker faced a "great challenge" over the U.N. peace plan.
But he added thatr Baker's diplomatic experience, political weight and his backing by the U.N. Security Council and international community would enable him to answer the challenge.
